title: The Martyrdom of Chrysogonus
subtitle: As Alban Butler tells it
source: Alban Butler, The Lives of the Fathers, Martyrs, and Other Principal Saints, vol. XI (London: John Murphy, 1815), November 24, p. 417, public domain. Read from the page images of archive.org's scan of the printing, word by word against a second scan of the same printing; where they differ, the printed page is followed. Butler's footnotes, the note of his sources under each heading and the running heads are left out, and his italics are set plain; the paragraphs are as printed.

sections.title: The Lives of the Saints, November 24
sections.citation: Alban Butler, The Lives of the Fathers, Martyrs, and Other Principal Saints, vol. XI (London: John Murphy, 1815), November 24, p. 417
paragraphs: The name of this holy martyr, who was apprehended at Rome, but beheaded at Aquileia in the persecution of Dioclesian, occurs in the canon of the mass, and is mentioned in the ancient Calendar of Carthage of the fifth century, and in all Western Martyrologies since that time. The church in Rome of which he is titular saint, is mentioned in a council held by pope Symmachus, and in the epistles of St. Gregory the Great; it gives title to a cardinal priest. The head of St. Chrysogonus is shewn there in a rich case; but his body is at Venice.
